clue.text: Dubious deal on defender

indicators.note: in an across entry one piece placed on another follows it, so the second item comes after the first

blocks.note: in football and hockey a back is a defending player
a deal at cards gives each player a hand

explanation.surface: A shady transaction involving a footballer, perhaps a bung paid to a centre-back.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is read in reverse clue order: the defender comes first and the deal is placed on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Backhand as an adjective is a variant of backhanded, meaning indirect, ambiguous or of questionable sincerity.

clue.text: Alliance lacks power to make law

indicators.note: to lack something is to be without it, so a letter goes missing

blocks.note: a pact is a formal agreement or alliance
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A coalition in parliament has too little clout to pass legislation.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove P from PACT to leave ACT.
explanation.definitionFit: An Act of Parliament is a statute, a piece of legislation passed formally by a legislature.

clue.text: Colouring agent in jelly that's provocative

indicators.note: one thing sitting inside another is enclosed by it

blocks.note: ink is a pigmented fluid used to colour
K-Y is a well-known brand of lubricating jelly

explanation.surface: Some dye in a jelly makes it racy, a cheeky nod to an adult product.
explanation.walkthrough: KY stands for K-Y Jelly, a personal lubricant, which fits the saucy definition. INK goes between its two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinky describes behaviour that is sexually daring or unconventional, hence suggestive and provocative.

clue.text: Bearing responsibility for clue type solvers can crack

blocks.note: first meaning: accountable to someone
second meaning: capable of being solved, as a clue is

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning is playful: a clue that solvers can crack is one that can be solved, literally able to be responded to correctly.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means accountable, and also literally capable of receiving a correct reply, as a solvable puzzle does.

clue.text: Rubbish parade Bristol hosts

indicators.note: to host is to have guests inside, so the letters sit within the phrase

blocks.note: found spanning the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A street procession in Bristol leaves litter behind, or is itself dismissed as rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: Look at the join: paraDE BRIStol.
explanation.definitionFit: Debris is scattered waste, broken fragments and litter left behind, which is rubbish.

clue.text: Seasoned actor provides well established benefit

blocks.note: something old has long been in place
a pro is an advantage, as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: An experienced performer brings solid value to a production.
explanation.walkthrough: PRO as advantage comes from the phrase pros and cons.
explanation.definitionFit: An old pro is a veteran with long experience in a trade, such as a stage performer who knows every trick.

clue.text: Slick and regularly social yankee

indicators.note: at regular intervals means taking every other letter

blocks.note: second, fourth and sixth letters
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A smooth-talking American who is out and about socialising a lot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yankee' looks like an American person but is just the radio code word for Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Oily describes someone ingratiatingly smooth, and literally a surface coated in grease, both senses of slick.

clue.text: Dylan side reworked will create wrath perhaps

indicators.note: something reworked has been redone in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Remixing a Bob Dylan track would enrage his fans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Side' suggests a record's side, but it only supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrath is one of the seven deadly sins; 'perhaps' shows the definition is an example, alongside pride, greed and envy.

clue.text: It's simple to deploy army under it

indicators.note: to deploy troops is to arrange them in position, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the eleven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A general remarks that positioning troops beneath something is easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deploy' fits the army surface so naturally that it hides its job as the rearranging signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudimentary means basic or elementary, involving only the most fundamental and uncomplicated elements.

clue.text: Impedes risky undertakings

blocks.note: first meaning: holds back growth or development
second meaning: daring feats

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a verb, the second a plural noun; the same word serves both.
explanation.definitionFit: To stunt is to hinder growth, and stunts are dangerous acrobatic or publicity feats performed for show.

clue.text: Posts put up backward slob, full of fat

indicators.note: going backward means reading from the end to the start
something full of stuff holds it inside

blocks.note: taken as written
lard is pig fat

explanation.surface: Someone scrawls online about an overweight, backward lazybones.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'put up' is not a turnaround signal; it belongs with 'Posts' as the definition, and 'backward' does the reversing.
explanation.definitionFit: Bollards are short sturdy posts erected in the street or on a quay to block vehicles or tie ropes.

clue.text: Lose pay in travelling around this island region

indicators.note: moving about from place to place suggests the letters wandering into a new order

blocks.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A warning that you will go unpaid while backpacking round the South Pacific islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Travelling around' fits the tourist picture, which hides that it is scrambling the three words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Polynesia is the vast Pacific area of scattered islands including Hawaii, Samoa, Tonga and French territories.

clue.text: Device first to be used if computer stops working?

definitions.text: Device first to be used if computer stops working?

blocks.clueFragment: Device first to be used if computer stops working?
blocks.note: surface reading: a gadget to reach for when a machine breaks down, like a repair tool

blocks.clueFragment: Device first to be used if computer stops working?
blocks.note: setter's reading: the standard fix of turning the machine off and back on again

explanation.walkthrough: Every help desk's first advice is to turn it off and on again, so the control you use first is the power button.
explanation.definitionFit: The control that toggles power is the first thing you reach for when a frozen computer needs restarting.

clue.text: Choice by bishop is sound

indicators.note: one thing standing by another is placed next to it

blocks.note: a plum job or role is the choicest one
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop's selection is judged to be a wise one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective meaning sensible, but it is the verb for measuring depth.
explanation.definitionFit: To plumb water is to measure its depth with a weighted line, which sailors call sounding.

clue.text: Demonstrating about exhibition that's been cancelled

blocks.note: a showing is a display or screening
an event that is off has been called off

explanation.surface: Protesters march about an art exhibition that was scrapped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Demonstrating about' suggests a protest, but here it means parading one's skills around.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing off is flaunting abilities or possessions, displaying them about the place to draw attention.

clue.text: Expense of turning around design

indicators.note: turning something round swaps its front and back, so the two halves change places

blocks.note: a layout is a plan or design

explanation.surface: The cost involved in reworking a plan.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the answer is not reversed letter by letter: the word's two halves swap places as whole chunks.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlay is money spent, the amount laid out on something, which is an expense.

clue.text: Identical line contributed to ruler showing star quality

indicators.note: something contributed to another is put into it

blocks.note: twin items are identical
a king is a ruler
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A lookalike who shares the monarch's line has charisma.
explanation.walkthrough: The line goes inside the ruler just after its first letter, and the identical piece stands in front of the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Stars twinkle in the night sky, so to be twinkling is literally to behave the way a star does.

clue.text: Elected to store pipe in empty cabin

indicators.note: an emptied word loses its contents, leaving only its outside letters
storing something means keeping it inside

blocks.note: first and last letters
a hose is a flexible pipe

explanation.surface: Someone decided to keep a pipe in a vacant hut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pipe' suggests a smoker's pipe; it is a garden hose.
explanation.definitionFit: Elected and chosen are synonyms, both meaning picked or selected, as by a vote.

clue.text: Delicate edges in finer imperial livery

indicators.note: the edges of a word are its outermost letters at each end

blocks.note: first and last letters
first and last letters
first and last letters

explanation.surface: Fine trimming on the borders of an ornate royal uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Edges' suits lace trimming, which hides that it selects the outer letters of three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Frilly means decorated with frills, lacy and dainty, so it suggests something fine and delicate.

clue.text: Country artist holds spellbinding instrument

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it inside

blocks.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist
a magic wand is used to cast spells

explanation.surface: A country music performer plays a mesmerising instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country artist' reads as one phrase, a singer, but 'Country' is the definition on its own. The instrument is a tool, not a musical one.
explanation.definitionFit: Rwanda is a small landlocked nation in east-central Africa.

clue.text: Something that can be added to Pennine town

blocks.note: first meaning: an optional extra fitted on, written as two words
second meaning: a town in Greater Manchester

explanation.walkthrough: Bolton is a large town in north-west England near the Pennine hills. A bolt-on is an accessory attached later.
explanation.definitionFit: A bolt-on is an add-on component, and Bolton is a mill town on the western edge of the Pennines.

clue.text: Conscious about what all kings expect initially

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so each word gives its opening letter

blocks.note: the opening letters of these five words

explanation.surface: A monarch is fully aware of what all royals demand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like a linking preposition, but it supplies the first letter too.
explanation.definitionFit: To be conscious is to be alert and not asleep, which is the state of being awake.

clue.text: Doesn't overreact when losing toys

blocks.note: a team losing a game is down
to toy with something is to play with it

explanation.surface: A calm child doesn't throw a tantrum when their toys go missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toys' looks like a plural noun but is a verb, and 'losing' means behind in a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: To downplay a matter is to minimise it, treating it as less important instead of making a fuss.

clue.text: America supports group position taken by yogis

indicators.note: in a down entry a support sits underneath, so it comes second

blocks.note: a lot is a group or batch
US is short for United States of America

explanation.surface: The United States backs a collective that practises yoga poses.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the supporting piece goes underneath, so America comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: The lotus is the cross-legged seated pose in yoga, feet resting on opposite thighs, used for meditation.

clue.text: Bloody choice between sides in galaxy

indicators.note: the sides of a word are its two outermost letters
something placed between two things sits inside them

blocks.note: first and last letters
or is the word that offers a choice

explanation.surface: A grim decision between warring factions across the galaxy, like a space-opera battle.
explanation.walkthrough: OR, the word of alternatives, sits between G and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Gory means covered in blood or full of violent bloodshed, as a bloody scene is.

clue.text: Remove tear in strapping

indicators.note: one thing in another is enclosed by it

blocks.note: stout and strapping both mean sturdily built
a rip is a tear

explanation.surface: Take away a torn section of webbing or strapping material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strapping' looks like a noun, straps; it is the adjective for burly.
explanation.definitionFit: To strip out is to take out or clear away, such as removing fittings from a room.

clue.text: Surpass available series

blocks.note: a product that is out has been released and can be had
a run is a series, as a run of wins

explanation.surface: A TV show that beats the other box sets on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: OUT as available is the sense of a new book being out.
explanation.definitionFit: To outrun is to go faster than and so leave behind, exceeding a rival.

clue.text: Coalition working away to establish learning establishment

indicators.note: something sent away is taken off and removed

blocks.note: a union is an alliance or coalition
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A political alliance labours to set up a college.
explanation.walkthrough: Take ON from the end of UNION.
explanation.definitionFit: Uni is the informal short form of university, an institution of higher education.

clue.text: Reluctant to acquire a horse so unkempt

indicators.note: acquiring something means taking it in

blocks.note: shy of doing something means reluctant to
taken as written
gee-gee is a childish word for a horse

explanation.surface: A hesitant buyer of a scruffy-looking pony.
explanation.walkthrough: GG is the nursery word gee-gee, standard crossword shorthand for a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaggy means covered in long, thick, untidy hair, so it describes something unkempt and scruffy.

clue.text: Dancing is fun fad – that's my final comment

indicators.note: dancing things move about and change position, so the letters shift

blocks.note: the eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses dancing as a passing craze and refuses to discuss it further.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuff' is a slangy clipping of enough.
explanation.definitionFit: The colloquial phrase declares that nothing more needs to be spoken, closing a discussion as a last word.
